title: Erdős #1018 Non-Planar Subgraph — Sorry Completion & Compile Repair

problemStatement.formal: Complete outstanding sorries in Proofs/Erdos1018Problem.lean (Erdős #1018: dense graphs contain small non-planar subgraphs, Kostochka–Pyber 1988).
problemStatement.plain: The main formalization file for Erdős #1018 had 7 sorries and (under Mathlib 4.26) no longer compiled. Goal: repair compilation and discharge whatever sorries follow from the stated axioms.
whyMatters: A broken gallery entry misrepresents the project's verified status; repairing it and proving a real lemma both count as concrete progress.

proven: superlinear_forces_nonplanar is now fully proved from the planar_linear_bound axiom: for ε>0 there is N with card V ≥ N ⇒ any ε-dense graph is non-planar. Threshold N = ⌈3^(1/ε)⌉+1; core inequality n^(1+ε)=n·n^ε ≤ 3n forces n^ε ≤ 3, contradicting n^ε > (3^(1/ε))^ε = 3.

Compile repair: the file did not build on Mathlib 4.26 (missing rpow instance HPow ℝ ℝ, unknown Nat.ceil, and a universe metavariable in erdos_1018_question). Fixed by importing Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real + Algebra.Order.Floor.Semiring and quantifying existsBoundingConstant over Type (universe 0).
Same repairs applied to the byte-identical Stubs/Erdos1018Problem.lean; both targets build cleanly.

insights: The file was a broken gallery entry: it failed to compile under Mathlib 4.26 (HPow ℝ ℝ unsynthesized, unknown Nat.ceil, universe metavariable) despite meta claiming 260-line/7-sorry axiomatized status — a false-verified hazard for auditors.

The universe metavariable came from a def whose body applies a Type*-polymorphic def while its own signature (: Prop) binds no universe; pinning the inner ∀ to Type removes the metavar without weakening the mathematics.

superlinear_forces_nonplanar is the conceptual heart of 'why the answer is YES': super-linear density n^(1+ε) exceeds the planar edge budget 3n-6, so density alone (via planar_linear_bound) already forces global non-planarity — the hard part is only the *small subgraph* localization (Kostochka-Pyber, still axiomatized).

Planarity can be defined combinatorially via the Kuratowski characterization (isPlanar := no K5/K33 subdivision); this turns kuratowski_theorem/K5_nonplanar/K33_nonplanar from axioms into theorems WITHOUT needing Mathlib topological planarity. The equivalence with topological planarity is Kuratowski itself, taken as definition — honest, not a proof of Kuratowski.

containsSubdivision has a clean sorry-free definition: injective branch map phi:W->V + a G-path between phi a, phi b for each H-edge, with paths being IsPath, interiors avoiding branch vertices, and pairwise internal disjointness (Diestel topological-minor def). self_containsSubdivision (identity branch map, length-1 paths) gives K5/K33 non-planarity trivially.

Lean 4.26 auto-includes section instance vars [Fintype V][DecidableEq V] into defs mentioning V, breaking polymorphic reuse on induced-subgraph subtype ↥S (failed to synthesize DecidableEq ↥S); fix = `omit [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] in` before each planarity def/theorem.

BLOCKER SHARPENED (researcher-6, 2026-07-12): the concrete isEmbeddableConc H 2 (Erdos1018OQ04Incomplete01.lean) unfolds, for 2-uniform H, to a straight-line NON-CROSSING drawing (convexHull of a 2-edge = its segment; separation ⟹ disjoint edges have disjoint segments, shared-vertex edges meet only at that vertex). Two genuine gaps, both absent from Mathlib v4.26: (1) the sole remaining sorry planar_graphs_edge_bound (|E| ≤ 3n) needs the Euler-formula planar edge bound; (2) the missing K5_not_planar (¬isEmbeddableConc K5 2) reduces to the GEOMETRIC Erdos-Szekeres / Happy-Ending lemma (any 5 points in general position contain a convex quadrilateral, whose diagonals are crossing K5-edges violating separation) PLUS a collinear-degenerate case. Mathlib HAS radon_partition (Analysis/Convex/Radon.lean) but it is INSUFFICIENT alone: applied to 4 points it can return a (1,3) partition (point inside a triangle) which yields NO pair of crossing independent edges; forcing the (2,2) crossing case is exactly the convex-quadrilateral (Erdos-Szekeres) statement, which Mathlib lacks (it has only the monotone-subsequence Erdos-Szekeres, not the geometric one).

The excess of Kₙ's edge count over Euler's planar bound is exact and structured: C(n,2) − (3n−6) = C(n−3,2) = (n−3)(n−4)/2 for n≥3 (excess_eq). This is 0 exactly at n∈{3,4} (the boundary planar cases) and grows quadratically for n≥5, re-deriving the n=5 threshold. More robustly, C(n,2) is superlinear (completeEdges_superlinear), so the counting obstruction does not depend on Euler's specific coefficient 3 — Kₙ overtakes any linear edge bound.
